content: How does Raft conduct leader election when a follower times out?

### SOURCE-BACKED ANSWER
According to the course materials, Raft decomposes consensus into three independent subproblems, one of which is Leader Election (📄 Page 3). If a follower receives no communication over an election timeout, it transitions to the Candidate state and requests votes via RequestVote RPCs (📄 Page 3).

content: Explain Lamport logical clocks formula and timestamp updating

### SOURCE-BACKED ANSWER
Lamport Logical Clocks assign a monotonically increasing integer timestamp C(e) to every event. If event a happens before b within the same process, then C(a) < C(b). When a message is received, the receiver updates its clock using the formula: max(C(receive), C(send)) + 1 (📄 Page 2).

content: What are the foundational definitions and structural properties in distributed systems?

According to the uploaded course materials, foundational definitions, invariants, and structural properties are extracted directly from the Distributed Systems Principles Textbook (📄 Page 1). Furthermore, the Brewer CAP Theorem defines key structural properties of distributed data stores, stating they can simultaneously provide at most two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance (📄 Page 5).
